title: Invariance under Equal Register States
statement: Let $x$ be a Boolean word, let $B$ be a natural number, let $l$ be a program label, let $p$ be a rational number, and let $\sigma,\sigma'$ be register states. If $\sigma=\sigma'$ and the probabilistic semantics property with parameter $p$ holds for the initial configuration formed from $\sigma'$ at label $l$, then it holds for the initial configuration formed from $\sigma$ at label $l$.
hypotheses_covered: The probabilistic semantics property with parameter $p$ holds for the initial configuration formed from $\sigma'$ at label $l$
replaced:
Let $x$ be a bit string, $B\in\mathbb{N}$, $\ell$ a machine label, $p\in\mathbb{Q}$, and
$\sigma,\sigma'$ register records. If $\sigma=\sigma'$ and the stated probabilistic
semantics property holds for the initial configuration formed from $\sigma'$, then it
also holds for the initial configuration formed from $\sigma$.
